introScript:
Ladies and gentlemen, representing Pugwash, Nova Scotia…

He is the man who started the road to the Tournament of Champions.

A proud Team Nova Scotia competitor with national-stage experience through the NDFC pathway, he brought veteran composure, heavy scoring, and Cumberland County pride into the Atlantic Amateur Darts Series.

At Event 1, he made history by becoming the first-ever AADS Series 1 Champion and the first player to punch his ticket to the Tournament of Champions.

A true veteran, a power scorer, and the man they call **Power House**…

Ladies and gentlemen, make some noise for your **AADS Event 1 Champion**…

**Tom "Power House" Holden!**

Ladies and gentlemen, representing Sussex, New Brunswick…

He has been carrying New Brunswick darts pride since his youth career.

A former Youth Team New Brunswick player and 2012 National Youth Championship joint bronze medalist, he has grown into a proven Team NB competitor with the intensity, emotion, and finishing power to take over a match.

At Event 2, he battled through the field and claimed his place among the champions.

He is dangerous, aggressive, and never backs down when the pressure rises.

Ladies and gentlemen, make some noise for your **AADS Event 2 Champion**…

**Kyle "The Animal" Gray!**

Ladies and gentlemen, representing Riverview, New Brunswick…

He is one of the brightest young talents in Atlantic Canadian darts.

A Canadian National Youth Champion, a Team Canada representative at the WDF World Cup, and a Phoenix-sponsored player mentored by Jeff "The Silencer" Smith, he has already proven himself on national and international stages.

At Event 3, he brought precision, patience, and confidence to the oche, capturing his AADS title and earning his place in the Tournament of Champions.

Calm under pressure, locked in on the target, and built for the big moment…

Ladies and gentlemen, make some noise for your **AADS Event 3 Champion**…

**Tyler "The Sniper" Cyr!**

Ladies and gentlemen, representing Cocagne, New Brunswick…

He is one of the most accomplished players in this championship field.

A Team New Brunswick standout, a Team Canada representative, and a player who has carried the Canadian flag onto the WDF World Cup stage, he brings international experience every time he steps to the line.

At the Korea Open, he delivered one of the rarest moments in darts — a match-winning 9-darter on the world stage.

At Event 4, he brought that same championship quality to the AADS and earned his place in the Tournament of Champions.

Ladies and gentlemen, make some noise for your **AADS Event 4 Champion**…

**Darrell "Dee" Cormier!**

Ladies and gentlemen, representing Nova Scotia…

He is one of the biggest momentum stories in the Tournament of Champions field.

Coming through the Nova Scotia qualifier pathway, he showed his form as an AADS Event 3 quarter-finalist before returning with something to prove.

With a joint 3rd-place finish at the NDFC Atlantic Open and high-performance moments including a 14-dart leg against Rhyder Oliver, he has shown he can catch fire when the pressure is at its highest.

At Event 5, he turned momentum into a championship and punched his ticket to the Series 1 finale.

Ladies and gentlemen, make some noise for your **AADS Event 5 Champion**…

**Drake Berry!**

Ladies and gentlemen, representing New Brunswick…

He entered the Atlantic Amateur Darts Series as the final major test of Series 1.

A proven NDFC national-stage competitor and New Brunswick heavyweight, he came into Event 6 with serious credentials, including a strong round-robin performance at the NDFC Canadian Nationals and a perfect 5–0 group-stage run at the Debbie Mullin Memorial.

Then, in his AADS debut, with the final Tournament of Champions seat on the line, he won the whole event.

He is the late arrival, the final qualifier, and the man known as **The Final Boss**.

Ladies and gentlemen, make some noise for your **AADS Event 6 Champion**…

**Rob Sibbick!**
